brief: Three regressions of WP27 and WP28, found by the H verifier (`verify-b3-r1-H.md`, ‘Regressions’). Everything else in WP26–WP28 came back fixed: don't change it. Line numbers are from that note, after WP28.

Change `:22` to `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(language, { weekday: "long" })`, which gives ‘Tuesday’, «martes», «dimarts», and update the comment at `:18-19` to say the sentence uses the full weekday and the cards their own short one. The cards' `day` formatter (`:23-27`) keeps `weekday: "short"`: don't touch the cards.

WEB-716, today and one o'clock: when the reset falls on the visitor's current local date (`resetAt.toDateString() === new Date().toDateString()`), say ‘today’ instead of the weekday (‘on Monday’ read on a Monday sounds like next week). Spanish and Catalan say «a la 1:30», not «a las/les 1:30», when the hour shown is 1: take it from `formats.time.formatToParts(resetAt)`, the part whose `type` is `hour`, value `"1"`. Replace the single `triesUsed` string with four sentences, chosen in `triesUsedLine` (`:424-428`); `triesUsedLater` (`:428`, no reset time) stays as it is. In `types.ts:159`: `triesUsed: { onDay: string; onDayAtOne: string; today: string; todayAtOne: string };`. Copy, exact (EN / ES / CA):

`onDay`: `You’ve used this demo’s 3 tries. You can try again on {weekday} at {time}.` / `Ya has usado los 3 intentos de esta demo. Podrás volver a probar el {weekday} a las {time}.` / `Ja has fet servir els 3 intents d’aquesta demo. Hi podràs tornar a provar {weekday} a les {time}.`

`onDayAtOne`: `You’ve used this demo’s 3 tries. You can try again on {weekday} at {time}.` / `Ya has usado los 3 intentos de esta demo. Podrás volver a probar el {weekday} a la {time}.` / `Ja has fet servir els 3 intents d’aquesta demo. Hi podràs tornar a provar {weekday} a la {time}.`

`today`: `You’ve used this demo’s 3 tries. You can try again today at {time}.` / `Ya has usado los 3 intentos de esta demo. Podrás volver a probar hoy a las {time}.` / `Ja has fet servir els 3 intents d’aquesta demo. Hi podràs tornar a provar avui a les {time}.`

`todayAtOne`: `You’ve used this demo’s 3 tries. You can try again today at {time}.` / `Ya has usado los 3 intentos de esta demo. Podrás volver a probar hoy a la {time}.` / `Ja has fet servir els 3 intents d’aquesta demo. Hi podràs tornar a provar avui a la {time}.` (English has no article, so its AtOne sentences equal the others.) The ‘today’ and ‘a la’ variants are the reviewer's copy; list their Catalan in your notes for a native read. The same line shows in the tries-used stage (`:720-731`) and after a last-try result (`.voice-again-later`, `:695`); both use `triesUsedLine`, so both change. Never write ‘tomorrow’: WP29 scans the demo for it.

WEB-717 (R1H-2, S2): after a refused recording (`audio_length`, `invalid_audio`, `too_large`), the panel shows the filled ‘Tap to talk’ circle and, under it, a filled ‘Done’ that resends the same refused recording (`:619-633` renders whenever `mode === "text" || (audio && !listening)`; `submit` never clears `audio` on failure, `:368-381`). Done now means ‘stop and send’, so it makes no sense when nothing is recording. Do this: (1) In `submit`, track a local `let retry = false`, set to true where the code calls `setRetryPending(true)` or `setRetryPending(data.code === "processing" || response.status === 503)` with a true value (both the `!response.ok` branch and the `catch` for `TimeoutError`/`TypeError`). In the `catch`, when `mode === "voice"` and `!retry`, call `setAudio(null)`: only ‘Tap to talk’ remains. (2) Render that block's ‘Done’ only in typed mode (`mode === "text"`), exactly as it is today, with its `pending` hint. (3) In voice mode, when `retryPending && audio && !listening`, render in its place one filled button, `className="button voice-retry"`, labelled with a new string `tryAgain`: `Try again` / `Reintentar` / `Torna-ho a provar` (the app's words, in the conventions), with the same `disabled={unavailable}` and `onClick={() => setPending(true)}`. It resends through the existing `requestId` and `retryPending` path, so the server returns the kept request without using a try (`src/lib/voice/store.ts:94`). `record()` already clears `retryPending` and `audio`, so tapping ‘Tap to talk’ instead starts afresh.

WEB-717 and WP29: WP29 (not run yet) also plans a filled ‘Try again’ (`tryAgain`) that resends through `retryPending`, for the typed mode, ‘Stop waiting’, the offline and gateway errors and the security check. Name the key `tryAgain` and the class `voice-retry` so WP29 reuses them rather than adding a second one. Don't build WP29's parts here: no ‘Stop waiting’, no new error messages, no change to the 55 s timeout, the server's message text or the security check.

WEB-718 (R1H-3, S1): the hidden `role="status"` (`.voice-status`, `:485-487`) keeps ‘Understanding…’ after the answer (set at `:326`, never cleared), so a screen reader reading down the result hears it before the heading. In `submit`'s `finally` (`:376-381`), add `setAnnouncement("")`. The result heading or the error alert already takes focus and speaks for itself. Leave the waiting stage's own `role="status"` line (`:518-520`) to WP29, which deletes it.

Tests: update what pins the old behaviour. In `tests/support/ux-voice.ts`, any voice scenario that resends with `#voice .voice-submit` after a failed recording uses `.voice-retry` (only where the failure is retryable) or records again; `submit()` (`:360-364`) stays the typed-mode helper. In `tests/voice.spec.ts`, tests that read the tries-used line expect the full weekday. Put the new acceptance tests in `tests/ux-web-voice.spec.ts`. Stub `resetAt`, and fix the page's clock and time zone (`page.clock`, `timezoneId: "Europe/Madrid"`) so the weekday and ‘today’ are certain. Compare times with whitespace normalised: ICU writes a narrow no-break space before ‘PM’.

Don't touch: the result's layout and order (WP28), the record button's look and focus, the capture stage's privacy line, the badge, `voice.css` (no style is needed: `.voice-retry` uses `.button`), the other session's line 396.

You can try again on Tuesday at 5:00 PM.” / «Ya has usado los 3 intentos de esta demo. Podrás volver a probar el martes a las 17:00.» / «Ja has fet servir els 3 intents d’aquesta demo. Hi podràs tornar a provar dimarts a les 17:00.», and contains none of ‘Tue ’, ‘el mar ’, ‘dt.’.

packages.title: At 200% text on phones, the sticky header stays one row
packages.commit: Commits: `src/styles/global.css` holds only this run's changes (WP25's verifier: clean at the start of WP25), and the tests go in `tests/ux-web-global.spec.ts`. No held file is touched.
brief: WEB-715 (R1G-1, S1) is a side effect of WP25 (`verify-b3-r1-G.md`, ‘Regressions’). Now that text grows, at 390 × 664 with the browser's text at 200% the wordmark grows to 46 px and pushes ‘Menu’ onto a second row: the sticky header (`.site-header`, `global.css:259-265`; `.header-inner` wraps, `:266-274`) is about 127 px tall, 19% of the screen, and stays while scrolling. Renders: `home.en.mobile-text200.light.fold.png`, `home.es.mobile-text200.light.fold.png`, `privacy.es.mobile-text200.light.fold.png`.

Fix: the wordmark is a logotype, which WCAG 1.4.4 exempts from resizing. In `.brand` (`global.css:275-283`) change `font-size: 1.4375rem;` to `font-size: min(1.4375rem, 28px);`. At default text it stays 23 px (nothing changes); at 200% it stops at 28 px, so the logo (about 165 px) and the Menu button (about 147 px) fit one row in the 350 px container. Add a one-line comment: the wordmark is a logotype, capped so the sticky header stays one row at large text sizes (WCAG 1.4.4 exempts logotypes).

Leave the Menu label growing. Don't touch `.footer-top .brand` (`:888-890`, its own 1.375rem; the footer isn't sticky), `.brand-mark`, `min-height: 48px` (WEB-703), `.header-inner`, the breakpoints or `scroll-padding-top`. At 320 px wide with text at 200% a wrap is still acceptable.

Tests: in `tests/ux-web-global.spec.ts`, next to WP37's text200 checks, using the DevTools protocol as they do (`Page.setFontSizes`, standard 32, fixed 26), measured while the setting is live, run on the mobile project (390 × 664).
acceptance: Mobile project, on /, /es/, /ca/ and /es/privacy/ at 390 × 664 with the browser's default font size at 32 px (Page.setFontSizes, live), light and dark: `.site-header` is at most 90 px tall; the header's `.brand` and the Menu button (`.header-menu summary`) are on one row (their vertical centres within 4 px); the `.brand` text's computed font-size is 28 px and the Menu label's is 32 px; nothing scrolls sideways.
Same pages and setting: after going to `#questions` on the home (`/#questions`, `/es/#questions`, `/ca/#questions`), the top of `#questions-title` is at or below the header's bottom.
With default text, at 1440 × 1000 and 390 × 664: the header's `.brand` text is 23 px, as before. axe reports no violations on /, /es/ and /ca/, light and dark, both projects.
Visual (verifier): `home.en.mobile-text200.light.fold.png`, `home.es.mobile-text200.light.fold.png` and `privacy.es.mobile-text200.light.fold.png` show the logo and Menu on one row.
deviceChecks: An Android phone with Chrome and the system font size at its largest: the header is one row and doesn't cover a fifth of the screen while scrolling.
